title: Will the model fit (looks hard, is easy)
prompt_text: I want to run a 7-billion-parameter model in bfloat16 on a GPU with 12 GB of memory. Quantisation is not an option. The KV cache costs 0.5 MB per token per sequence at this model size, I want a 4,096-token context, and I was thinking of batch sizes of 1, 2 or 4. Activations are small enough to ignore. Which batch size should I use, and how much memory will be left over?

content:
Based on the constraints you provided, it is **mathematically impossible** to run this model on a 12 GB GPU, regardless of the batch size you choose.

Here is the breakdown of the memory requirements:

### 1. Model Weight Memory
A model with 7 billion parameters stored in `bfloat16` uses 2 bytes per parameter.
*   $7,000,000,000 \text{ parameters} \times 2 \text{ bytes} = 14,000,000,000 \text{ bytes}$
*   $14,000,000,000 \text{ bytes} \approx \mathbf{14\text{ GB}}$

Even before you load a single token or define a batch size, the weights alone require **14 GB** of VRAM. Your GPU only has **12 GB**. 

### 2. KV Cache Memory
Even if you had a large enough GPU to fit the weights, here is how the KV cache would scale based on your provided cost (0.5 MB per token per sequence) and a 4,096-token context:

*   **Per Sequence:** $4,096 \text{ tokens} \times 0.5\text{ MB/token} = 2,048\text{ MB} = \mathbf{2\text{ GB}}$
*   **Batch Size 1:** $14\text{ GB (weights)} + 2\text{ GB (cache)} = \mathbf{16\text{ GB}}$
*   **Batch Size 2:** $14\text{ GB (weights)} + 4\text{ GB (cache)} = \mathbf{18\text{ GB}}$
*   **Batch Size 4:** $14\text{ GB (weights)} + 8\text{ GB (cache)} = \mathbf{22\text{ GB}}$

### Summary Table

| Batch Size | Weights | KV Cache | Total Needed | Status (on 12 GB GPU) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | 14 GB | 2 GB | 16 GB | **-4 GB Deficit** |
| **2** | 14 GB | 4 GB | 18 GB | **-6 GB Deficit** |
| **4** | 14 GB | 8 GB | 22 GB | **-10 GB Deficit** |

### Conclusion
To run this model in `bfloat16` with a 4,096 context length at Batch Size 1, you would need a GPU with at least **16 GB** of VRAM (and realistically 18–20 GB to account for overhead and activations).

Since you ruled out quantization, your only options are to:
1. Use a GPU with more VRAM (e.g., 24 GB).
2. Reduce the context length significantly.
3. Use CPU offloading (which will be extremely slow).
